text:
Predicates:
Twins(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplets(x) ::: x is a triplet.
Siblings(x, y) ::: x has siblings y.
HangOutWith(x, y) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with y.
PlayWith(x, y) ::: x spends a lot of time playing with y.
DevelopBonds(x, y) ::: x develops strong bonds with y.
Complain(x) ::: x complains often.
SameAge(x, y) ::: x and y are the same age.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
FamilyMembers(x, y) ::: y is a family member of x.

Premises:
∀x ((Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x)) → (HangOutWith(x, Siblings(x)) ∧ PlayWith(x, Siblings(x)))) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x ((∃y SameAge(x, y)) → (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x))) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (Complain(x) → ∃y (SameAge(x, y))) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHome(x) → ¬∃y DevelopBonds(x, FamilyMembers(y))) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x ((HangOutWith(x, Siblings(x)) ∧ PlayWith(x, Siblings(x))) → ¬LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∧ DevelopBonds(luke, FamilyMembers) ⊕ ¬((Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∨ DevelopBonds(luke, FamilyMembers)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.

Conclusion:
HangOutWith(luke, Siblings(luke)) ∧ PlayWith(luke, Siblings(luke)) ::: Luke spends a lot of time hanging out and playing with his siblings.
